title: Uncovering Understanding-Generation Synergy in Native Unified Multimodal Models: From Representation, Task to System
headline: Synergy Between Understanding and Generation in Unified Multimodal Models Explored
tldr: This study examines how visual understanding and generation tasks interact within native unified multimodal models, analyzing their interplay at representation, task, and system levels. The results reveal that while synergy can exist, the two objectives may also compete for capacity, highlighting the need for balanced training strategies.
significance: Understanding the balance between comprehension and generation in multimodal models is crucial for designing more efficient and capable AI systems.

title: Observable- and state-selective prethermalization and bounds on prethermal lifetimes
headline: Prethermalization: When Energy Scale Separation Fails to Produce Long-Lived Plateaus
tldr: The study shows that merely having distinct energy scales does not guarantee a prethermal plateau. Certain observables can still relax rapidly, indicating that additional conditions are required for long-lived intermediate states.
significance: Understanding the precise conditions for prethermalization informs the design of experiments and the control of non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum systems.

title: Depth-1 expanders on the unitary group and applications
headline: Depth-1 Quantum Expanders Achieve Optimal Entanglement Gap in 1D Hamiltonians
tldr: We construct a constant-degree, constant-gap quantum expander realizable by depth‑1 1D circuits of Pauli and CNOT gates. This expander yields a family of frustration‑free 1D Hamiltonians whose ground‑state entanglement scales as Θ(Δ^{-1/2}), matching the conjectured optimal bound.
significance: It provides the first depth‑1 quantum expander with optimal entanglement‑gap scaling, bridging quantum complexity and many‑body physics.

title: Beyond Scores: Understanding LLM-as-a-Judge Mechanisms in Summarization Evaluation
headline: Decoding LLM Judges: How Language Models Score Summaries and Why It Matters
tldr: This study dissects how large language models evaluate summary quality, revealing the hidden decision process behind their ratings. By applying an eight-attack perturbation taxonomy across readability and adequacy, the authors show how specific linguistic changes influence model scores.
significance: Understanding LLM evaluation mechanisms is crucial for developing reliable automated metrics and improving NLG system training.

title: Singular Weak-Field Thermodynamics of 2D Superconductors
headline: Size-Dependent Lower Critical Field in Two-Dimensional Superconductors Reveals Singular Weak-Field Thermodynamics
tldr: In bulk 3D type-II superconductors, the lower critical field is a material constant, but in 2D systems it decreases with sample size. This study shows that the first vortex in a 2D disk appears at a field that scales inversely with area, making the lower critical field inherently size-dependent.
significance: Understanding size-dependent vortex nucleation in 2D superconductors is essential for designing nanoscale quantum devices and could impact future superconducting technologies.

title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?
headline: Evaluating LLMs on Component Lifecycle Reasoning in Dynamic Agent Harnesses with CordisBench
tldr: CordisBench presents 1,200 questions testing whether language models can track changes in software components and their dependencies during execution. The benchmark highlights the added reasoning burden of dynamic agent harnesses and offers a controlled setting for evaluating lifecycle reasoning.
significance: It provides the first systematic evaluation of LLMs' ability to manage component lifecycles, a critical capability for self-modifying agents.

title: UI-VISA: U-Net Initialized Vascular Image Segmentation Architecture
headline: UI-VISA: Enhancing Vascular Segmentation in DSA Images with U-Net Initialization
tldr: UI-VISA introduces a U-Net initialized architecture that improves continuity of thin vascular predictions in digital subtraction angiography. The model leverages explicit vessel connectivity constraints to reduce fragmentation and enhance segmentation accuracy.
significance: This approach addresses a key limitation in medical image segmentation, enabling more reliable vessel delineation for clinical analysis.

title: The Rise of Verbal Reinforcement Learning
headline: Verbal Reinforcement Learning: Harnessing Natural Language Feedback for AI Agents
tldr: Verbal Reinforcement Learning (VRL) uses natural language as a primary feedback channel, enabling agents to learn intent, preferences, and causal structure. This paper presents a unified framework and demonstrates VRL's potential across diverse tasks.
significance: VRL offers a scalable, interpretable method to align language models with human intent, potentially accelerating AI deployment.

title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
headline: Facet-0: A Foundation Model for Precise Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation Assembly
tldr: Facet-0 is a robotic foundation model that predicts contact outcomes and optimizes actions for sub-millimeter precision. It combines multimodal representation learning with reinforcement learning to handle compliant interactions and contact failures in real-world assembly.
significance: Facet-0 advances robotic manipulation by enabling robust, precise assembly at sub-millimeter tolerances through predictive contact modeling.

title: Mechanism Design for Alignment and Control
headline: Designing Incentives for Unknown AI Agents: Aligning Preferences and Capabilities
tldr: We propose a mechanism design framework that accounts for unknown preferences and capabilities of AI agents, ensuring both honesty and obedience. Using a one-sided imitation structure, we establish a revelation principle that characterizes implementable mechanisms.
significance: This framework enables reliable delegation of tasks to AI agents even when their internal states are hidden, advancing trustworthy AI deployment.

title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators
headline: StudentSim: Leveraging LLMs to Simulate Student Learning for Adaptive Tutoring
tldr: StudentSim trains large language models to act as student simulators, providing a scalable proxy for real learner data. This enables rapid evaluation of personalized tutoring strategies without costly human trials.
significance: By offering a realistic, data-driven simulation of student responses, StudentSim accelerates the development of effective, individualized AI tutoring systems.

title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing
headline: Proactive Thought Partners: AI Agents That Anticipate Writers' Needs and Enhance Creativity
tldr: This paper explores how AI can proactively support writers by offering context‑aware suggestions at the right moments. It outlines a design space for proactive thought partners, moving beyond generic autocomplete to personalized, timely assistance.
significance: By redefining AI assistance as a proactive thought partner, the study opens new avenues for more engaging and effective writing tools.

title: Strain-Tunable Spin Relaxation in Germanium from First Principles
headline: First-Principles Prediction of Strain-Tunable Spin Relaxation in Germanium for Quantum Devices
tldr: Using hybrid-functional band structures and fully relativistic electron-phonon interactions, we compute spin relaxation times in bulk germanium under strain. The results reveal a strong tunability of spin lifetimes, offering a pathway to optimize spin qubits without phenomenological assumptions.
significance: This work provides the first ab initio framework for engineering spin lifetimes in germanium, a key material for scalable quantum technologies.

title: Constant Individual Regret in General Games
headline: ECHO-OFTRL Achieves Constant Individual Regret in Finite N-Player Games
tldr: The paper introduces ECHO-OFTRL, an optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader algorithm with an EMA cascade that eliminates the polylogarithmic horizon dependence in constant individual regret. It guarantees efficient, decentralized convergence for any finite normal-form game under full-information feedback.
significance: This work provides the first horizon-independent regret bounds for decentralized learning in general games, enabling faster and more reliable equilibrium convergence.

title: SUN: Persistent Programs For Language-Grounded Control-to-Learning-to-Real Policies
headline: SUN: Bridging Control and Learning with Language-Grounded Persistent Programs for Long-Horizon Manipulation
tldr: The SUN framework integrates typed, language-grounded programs to unify model-based control and learned policies for long-horizon manipulation tasks. By preserving task semantics, SUN eliminates hand-crafted rewards and ensures policies remain faithful to verified control behavior.
significance: SUN enables reliable, interpretable, and efficient policy learning that stays aligned with formal control objectives, advancing long-horizon robotic manipulation.

title: Evolution of Cosmic String Loops under Gravitational Backreaction
headline: Gravitational Backreaction Alters Cosmic String Cusp Signals in the Early Universe
tldr: Cosmic string loops generate strong gravitational wave bursts at cusps, but gravitational backreaction smooths the string, reducing burst amplitude. This alters the strain spectrum and affects gravitational wave search strategies.
significance: Understanding backreaction is crucial for accurate predictions of gravitational wave signals from cosmic strings.

title: Trinomial containment in polynomial ideals is undecidable
headline: Undecidability of Trinomial Containment in Polynomial Ideals via MRDP Reduction
tldr: We show that deciding whether an ideal in a polynomial ring over Q contains a trinomial is undecidable. By constructing an ideal from an integer polynomial, we reduce the existence of integral zeros to trinomial containment, invoking the MRDP theorem.
significance: This result establishes a new class of undecidable problems in computational algebra, linking Diophantine equations to ideal membership questions.

title: Agentic research is oxymoronic
headline: Agentic AI in Research: An Oxymoron That Threatens Scientific Trust
tldr: Agentic large language models can bypass human interpretation, potentially eroding trust in scientific findings. This raises concerns about the reliability of AI-driven research outputs.
significance: The article highlights the risk that fully autonomous AI research may undermine confidence in scientific literature.

title: BRF-GS: Hyperspectral Bidirectional Reflectance Factor Modeling and Image Generation Based on 3D Gaussian Splatting
headline: Efficient Hyperspectral BRF Modeling with 3D Gaussian Splatting for Multi-Angle Terrestrial Surface Imaging
tldr: This study introduces a novel method for modeling bidirectional reflectance factor (BRF) using 3D Gaussian Splatting, enabling rapid generation of multi-angle hyperspectral imagery. By replacing computationally intensive radiative transfer solvers with efficient point‑cloud rendering, the approach significantly reduces processing time while maintaining high fidelity.
significance: The method accelerates hyperspectral remote sensing analysis, facilitating real‑time applications in environmental monitoring and land cover classification.

title: Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations
headline: Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations
tldr: This work establishes sharp theoretical bounds on how well neural networks whose parameters are generated from low-dimensional latent vectors can approximate target functions. The results show that affine latent parameterizations achieve near-optimal approximation rates while dramatically reducing parameter count.
significance: It provides a rigorous foundation for designing efficient large-scale models that can be generated from compact latent codes, bridging theory and practical parameter-efficient architectures.

title: QGPINNs: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Nonlocal Differential Equations on Quantum Graphs
headline: QGPINNs: Neural Networks Solve Nonlocal Differential Equations on Quantum Graphs
tldr: We introduce QGPINNs, a PyTorch-based physics-informed neural network framework that approximates solutions on each edge of a quantum graph. A unified graph-based loss enforces governing equations, enabling efficient numerical solutions for nonlocal differential equations.
significance: QGPINNs provide a scalable, open-source tool for solving complex nonlocal PDEs on network structures, bridging physics, machine learning, and quantum graph theory.

title: A Similarity Theorem and Its Breakdown in Atomic Black Hole Accretion
headline: Similarity Theorem in Atomic Black Hole Accretion and Its Breakdown
tldr: The study demonstrates that atomic gas around a point-mass follows an exact similarity scaling with mass and density, preserving key dimensionless profiles over time. However, this similarity fails when certain radiation and feedback processes are introduced, revealing limits to the model.
significance: It provides a fundamental scaling framework for modeling accretion flows, but also delineates its applicability limits in realistic astrophysical environments.

title: Bounds for inertialess dynamo
headline: Inertialess Dynamo Bounds in Rapidly Rotating Convection: New Theoretical Limits
tldr: We derive necessary conditions for instantaneous dynamo action in rotating convection without inertia or viscosity. The study links magnetic evolution to an inertialess force balance, extending kinematic dynamo theory.
significance: These bounds provide critical insight into magnetic field generation in planetary cores and astrophysical plasmas.

title: Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation
headline: Renormalization-Guided Upscaling Enhances Lattice Field Generation with Normalizing Flow and Rapid Rethermalization
tldr: We present a renormalization-group guided machine-learning algorithm that uses a perfect blocking construction to generate equilibrated long-distance modes, then reconstructs short-distance details via a conditional normalizing flow, and finally applies brief rethermalization to remove residual errors. In 2D φ^4 theory at criticality, the method achieves accurate field generation with reduced computational cost.
significance: This approach provides a scalable, physics-informed framework for generating high-fidelity lattice field configurations, potentially accelerating critical phenomena studies.

title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
headline: Efficient Lattice Field Generation via Renormalization-Guided Inverse Blocking for Accurate Simulations
tldr: We introduce a renormalization-group guided inverse blocking algorithm that reconstructs fine-grained lattice configurations from coarse actions. Validation shows the method reproduces key observables with high fidelity while reducing computational cost.
significance: This approach provides a scalable, accurate tool for lattice field theory simulations, potentially accelerating research in high-energy physics.

title: Aero Hand Open: A Simulation-Ready Tendon-Driven Hand for Dexterous Manipulation Learning
headline: Aero Hand Open: Affordable Tendon-Driven Hand for Realistic Dexterous Manipulation
tldr: Aero Hand Open presents a low-cost, tendon-driven robotic hand that can be simulated and built with off-the-shelf components. Its design allows a single motor to drive multiple joints, enabling realistic dexterous manipulation for research and education.
significance: This hand democratizes access to advanced robotic manipulation research by reducing cost and complexity.

title: How Long-Range Tails Reshape Non-Hermitian Spectra
headline: Long-Range Hopping Rewrites Non-Hermitian Spectra Under Open Boundaries
tldr: Even infinitesimal long-range hoppings can drastically alter the spectrum and eigenstates of short-range non-Hermitian systems. This effect challenges the common truncation approximation used in realistic tight-binding models.
significance: The study reveals that truncating long-range interactions can lead to qualitatively incorrect predictions in non-Hermitian physics, impacting design and analysis of open quantum systems.

title: Learning a Size-Weight Frontier for Synthetic-Augmented Inference
headline: Balancing Synthetic Data and Real Observations for Reliable Statistical Inference
tldr: Synthetic data can boost inference when real data are scarce, but treating them as real can bias results. We propose a framework that quantifies synthetic augmentation by count and weight, enabling reliable inference across related tasks.
significance: This framework offers a principled way to integrate synthetic data, reducing bias and improving inference quality in data-limited settings.

title: Super-resolution Control of Two-dimensional Quantum Emitters
headline: Precise Spatial Control of 2D Quantum Emitters via Super-Resolution Techniques
tldr: Localized interlayer excitons in TMD heterobilayers act as quantum emitters with static dipole moments, enabling nanoscale charge sensing. This study demonstrates electrically tunable, spin-valley selective emitters with super-resolution spatial control, paving the way for probing correlated quantum phases.
significance: Enabling deterministic spatial placement of quantum emitters unlocks precise probing of quantum many-body states in adjacent layers.

title: Quantum Fourier transform toolbox
headline: New Quantum Fourier Transform Toolbox Enables Efficient Non-Abelian Group Circuits
tldr: We present a toolbox that constructs efficient QFT circuits for non-abelian groups using Mackey and Clifford theory. The framework supports rapid prototyping and benchmarking of quantum algorithms.
significance: This advances quantum algorithm design by providing scalable QFT implementations for previously intractable group families.

title: PULSAR: Pooled Unified Late-Interaction Search and Retrieval for Enterprise Visual Document RAG
headline: PULSAR: Vision-First Retrieval System for Enterprise Pitch Decks at Mubadala
tldr: PULSAR is a vision-first retrieval system that indexes page images of pitch decks and board packs, enabling instant search without costly OCR refreshes. Deployed at Mubadala Investment Company, it uses a frozen ColPali-style backbone for real-time, high-fidelity retrieval.
significance: PULSAR dramatically reduces latency and cost for visual document search, preserving chart detail for time-sensitive investment decisions.

title: Learning to Decode Concatenated Quantum Codes with Hierarchical Message Passing
headline: Neural Message Passing Boosts Decoding of Concatenated Quantum Hamming Codes
tldr: We propose a lightweight neural message-passing decoder for concatenated stabilizer codes, where soft beliefs flow bidirectionally across levels. Applied to the [[15,7,3]] quantum Hamming code, it achieves significantly higher error thresholds than existing bidirectional decoders.
significance: This work demonstrates that simple neural aggregation can dramatically improve quantum error correction thresholds, paving the way for more efficient quantum computing.

title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit
headline: Separating Persona and Execution for Auditable LLM Agents in Governed Environments
tldr: This paper introduces Persona‑Execution Separation, a pattern that splits an LLM agent’s persona and its execution into distinct trust domains linked by a governed contract bridge. It enables the persona to evolve freely while keeping stateful work auditable and traceable.
significance: It provides a scalable, cost‑effective way to balance flexibility and governance for LLM agents in regulated organizations.

title: Leading term strandings for webs
headline: Identifying Leading Term Strandings in sl_n Webs: A New Construction Approach
tldr: This paper introduces a method to identify leading term strandings in sl_n webs, which encode the dominant monomial of the invariant vector. By providing an algorithmic construction, it facilitates explicit computations in quantum group representation theory.
significance: The technique streamlines the extraction of leading terms, aiding both theoretical analysis and computational applications in quantum algebra.

title: High-order stabilized matrix-free simulation of rotating mixing devices using the Mortar Element Method
headline: High-Order Matrix-Free Simulation of Rotating Mixers via Mortar Element Method
tldr: We develop a high-order continuous Galerkin framework for rotating mixers, employing a matrix-free Navier-Stokes solver and Mortar Element domain decomposition. The method uses ALE to handle rotor-stator motion, enabling efficient, stabilized simulations of complex mixing devices.
significance: This approach enables accurate, scalable simulations of rotating mixers without assembling large matrices, improving design and optimization of industrial mixing processes.

title: misi: a Metric Inverted Sample Index
headline: MISI: Efficient Inverted Sample Index for Approximate Nearest-Neighbor Search in Metric Spaces
tldr: MISI introduces a lightweight inverted index that samples database points to enable fast approximate nearest-neighbor queries in any metric space. By representing each object with its nearest sample points and using IDF-weighted shared-neighbor voting, it achieves high recall with minimal verification cost.
significance: MISI offers a scalable, open-source solution that reduces ANN search time while maintaining accuracy across diverse metric spaces.

title: Learning a Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Without Hour-by-Hour Supervision: A Two-Site Retrospective Study
headline: Continuous Sepsis Severity Score Learned from Patient Trajectories Across Two Hospitals
tldr: We developed a continuous sepsis severity score using deep learning on longitudinal vital signs, without hourly labels, and validated it on 29,116 and 7,691 patients from two hospitals. The model outperformed existing fixed indices and offers a data‑driven alternative for real‑time clinical decision support.
significance: This study provides a scalable, data‑driven sepsis severity metric that can adapt to modern ICU populations and improve early detection.

title: Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR
headline: Weak-Model Guidance Enhances LLM Exploration in RLVR
tldr: RLVR improves LLM reasoning but reduces policy entropy, limiting coverage. Introducing weak-model guidance restores entropy and boosts pass@k.
significance: This method expands reasoning diversity in large language models without sacrificing performance.

title: Value distribution of multiplicative functions along linear fractional sequences
headline: Characterizing Limit Points of Multiplicative Functions on Linear Fractional Sequences
tldr: We provide a full description of the limit points of any unimodular multiplicative function evaluated on the rational values of a linear fractional transformation. The result hinges on the multiplicative recurrence of the resulting set and yields a complete classification.
significance: This work resolves a long-standing question about the asymptotic behavior of multiplicative functions on rational sequences, bridging analytic number theory and dynamical systems.

title: Retrieval Heads Meet Vision: Uncovering How VLMs Locate and Extract Visual Information
headline: Visual Retrieval Heads Reveal How VLMs Locate and Extract Image Regions
tldr: We show that vision‑language models contain visual retrieval heads that can locate image regions referenced by text. These heads enable the model to route visual evidence to the output, revealing a new mechanism for spatial reasoning.
significance: This discovery uncovers the internal mechanism behind VLMs’ ability to perform grounded language tasks, opening avenues for more interpretable and controllable multimodal AI.

title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: Constraints on the anisotropic screening and birefringence effects with DR6
headline: ATC Telescope Tightens Bounds on CMB Anisotropic Screening & Birefringence
tldr: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope’s DR6 observations provide the most stringent constraints yet on anisotropic screening caused by Thomson scattering of CMB photons. They also limit the rotation of CMB polarization due to cosmic birefringence, tightening bounds on parity‑violating physics beyond the Standard Model.
significance: These results sharpen constraints on early‑universe physics and potential new interactions that could leave imprints on the CMB.

title: Graded Ehrhart theory for hypersimplices
headline: Graded Ehrhart Theory for Hypersimplices: q-Ehrhart Series and Orbit Harmonics
tldr: We prove that the q-Ehrhart series of a hyperplane slice of a cube is a rational function with an explicit denominator satisfying q-reciprocity, confirming a conjecture of Reiner and Rhoades. We also find a generating set for the orbit harmonics ideal, yielding the Hilbert series and graded Frobenius characteristic of the quotient.
significance: This work resolves a conjecture in combinatorial geometry and provides new tools for studying orbit harmonics and graded Frobenius characteristics.

title: The JWST/NIRCam Scattered Light Disks GTO 2780 program: panchromatic coronagraphic imaging of the HD 10647, HD 32297, HD 61005, HD 107146, and HD 181327 debris disk systems
headline: JWST Reveals Fine Structures in Five Debris Disk Systems with NIRCam Coronagraphy
tldr: The James Webb Space Telescope’s NIRCam instrument captured high‑contrast, panchromatic images of five nearby debris disks, revealing intricate rings, gaps, and asymmetries that hint at unseen planets. These observations provide unprecedented detail on dust composition and dynamics, advancing our understanding of planetary system evolution.
significance: This study delivers the most detailed scattered‑light view of multiple debris disks, offering critical constraints on planet–disk interactions.

title: Free Novikov-Zinbiel algebra
headline: Constructing a Basis for Novikov‑Zinbiel Algebras via Graded Rational Functions
tldr: We consider a commutative associative algebra with an invertible derivation and define two operations that give a Novikov‑Zinbiel algebra. Using a graded model we represent monomials by rational functions and explicitly build a basis for the resulting space.
significance: This provides an explicit combinatorial description of Novikov‑Zinbiel algebras, facilitating further algebraic and representation‑theoretic investigations.

title: Monotonicity of the propagation speed with respect to the diffusion in a Lotka-Volterra competition-diffusion system
headline: Monotonicity of Propagation Speed in Lotka-Volterra Competition-Diffusion Systems
tldr: The study demonstrates how diffusion ratios influence the speed of traveling fronts in strongly competing species, revealing a smooth, monotonic relationship. This determines which species successfully invades the other's territory.
significance: Understanding diffusion-driven invasion dynamics informs ecological management and predictive modeling of species spread.

title: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
headline: MAELLE: Mechanistic Reaction Prediction via Discrete Flow Matching on Graph-Structured Electron Occupation
tldr: MAELLE introduces a novel mechanistic framework that predicts chemical reactions by modeling electron rearrangements as discrete flow matching on graph-structured electron occupancy. This approach moves beyond heuristic graph edits, enabling more accurate and interpretable reaction predictions.
significance: By directly modeling electron dynamics, MAELLE offers a more faithful representation of reaction mechanisms, potentially accelerating drug discovery and materials design.

title: Stochastic Estimation of Transduced Language Models
headline: Stochastic Estimation of Transduced Language Models via Finite-State Transducers for Target Strings
tldr: Transduced language models combine a pretrained source language model with a finite-state transducer to generate a language model over target strings. Estimating target prefix probabilities requires summing source probabilities over all source strings mapped to target prefixes, which can be computationally expensive.
significance: This approach enables efficient probabilistic modeling of transformed language outputs, bridging pretrained models and structured mapping.

title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners
headline: Assessing AI Model Security Scanners: Coverage, Failure Recovery, and Benchmarking
tldr: We benchmark three static AI model scanners—ModelScan, ModelAudit, and Fickling—on a synthetic corpus of 170 Pickle and PyTorch artifacts. The study reveals gaps in coverage and failure recovery, highlighting the need for standardized evaluation metrics.
significance: This work provides the first systematic evaluation of AI model security scanners, guiding developers toward more robust artifact safety practices.

title: Spectral Fingerprints of Gauge Theories on a Quantum Computer
headline: Quantum Spectral Sampling Unveils Gauge Theory Fingerprints, Enabling Precise Energy Landscape Mapping
tldr: We present an unbiased quantum algorithm that samples the spectrum of a Hamiltonian, enabling extraction of finite-resolution spectral distributions across the entire energy range. By focusing on specific spectral regions, the method reveals the full fingerprint of gauge theories, including ground state properties and excited state dynamics.
significance: This approach provides a scalable, quantum-enabled tool for probing complex gauge models, potentially accelerating discoveries in high-energy physics and quantum field theory.

title: UrbanGround: From Local Perception to Spatial Agency in a Real-Scale City
headline: UrbanGround: From Local Perception to Spatial Agency in Real-Scale City Navigation
tldr: UrbanGround introduces a sandbox environment to evaluate how multimodal large language models translate street-level perception into actionable navigation in real-scale cities. The study demonstrates current MLLM limitations and highlights the need for improved spatial reasoning capabilities.
significance: This work provides the first systematic benchmark for assessing urban agency in multimodal LLMs, guiding future research toward more reliable city-scale navigation.

title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
headline: CritICL: Efficient Inference-Time Reasoning for Small LLMs
tldr: CritICL introduces a lightweight inference-time framework that leverages small language model failure modes to boost reasoning accuracy. It achieves this without repeated generation or external verification, maintaining high efficiency.
significance: This work demonstrates that small LLMs can attain strong reasoning performance through inference-time adaptations, reducing computational overhead.

title: WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution
headline: WikiSkill: Turning Agent Experience into Reusable Skills for Continuous Learning
tldr: WikiSkill automatically extracts reusable skill modules from an agent's optimization history, enabling the agent to adapt and evolve its capabilities over time. By consolidating scattered insights into a persistent knowledge base, the system promotes systematic reuse and accelerates skill development.
significance: This approach bridges the gap between episodic learning and long-term knowledge accumulation, making AI agents more efficient and adaptable.

title: Distinguishing Quantum Capacitance Signatures of a Topological Majorana Wire from a Normal Wire Segment
headline: Quantum Capacitance Reveals Majorana Modes in Topological Superconducting Wires and Distinguishes Normal Segments
tldr: A quantum-dot interferometer measures the quantum capacitance of a superconducting wire, allowing detection of Majorana zero modes at its ends. The distinct resonance patterns and magnetic flux dependence differentiate a topological wire from a trivial normal segment.
significance: This technique provides a non-invasive probe to confirm Majorana modes, a key step toward topological quantum computing.

title: Tacet: A Language and Type System for Automatic Statistical Validity Accounting
headline: Tacet: Automating Statistical Validity with a Dedicated Language and Type System
tldr: Tacet introduces a programming language and type system that automatically tracks statistical validity across empirical comparisons. By encoding analysis structure, it enables rigorous multiple‑comparison correction without manual p‑value bookkeeping.
significance: This work provides a principled framework for ensuring statistical soundness in empirical computer science research, reducing false discoveries.

title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance
headline: SWE-Prime: Reducing Trajectory Volume Improves LLM Performance on Software Tasks
tldr: SWE-Prime demonstrates that selectively curating fewer, higher-quality agent trajectories yields superior fine-tuning of large language models for software engineering tasks. By filtering out redundant or risky steps, the approach achieves better performance with less data.
significance: This work challenges the assumption that more data always leads to better LLMs, offering a more efficient path to high-performing software engineering assistants.

title: TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization
headline: Test-Time Policy Optimization Enhancing LLM Reasoning Without Ground Truth for Large Models
tldr: This paper introduces Test-Time Policy Optimization (TTPO), a method that replaces reliance on ground-truth labels with majority-vote pseudo-labels to enable test-time training of large language models. TTPO improves mathematical reasoning performance while mitigating the fragility of pseudo-labels.
significance: TTPO offers a practical approach to adapt LLMs during inference, reducing dependency on labeled data and advancing real-time reasoning capabilities.

title: Proof of the AGT Conjecture at Generic $β$
headline: All-Level Proof of AGT Conjecture via Selberg Averages
tldr: The paper presents a complete proof of the four-point SU(2) AGT correspondence at generic β by establishing a factorization formula for Selberg averages of generalized Jack polynomials. It derives one-box matrix elements through a Jack limit of the Macdonald Pieri rule.
significance: It resolves a long-standing problem in mathematical physics by providing a rigorous foundation for the AGT correspondence at arbitrary deformation parameters.

title: Do User-Authored Permission Policies Improve Protection Against AI Agent Overreach?
headline: User-Authored Permission Policies Reduce AI Agent Overreach and Enhance Trust
tldr: AI agents can act across many services, but users often lack control. This study shows that allowing users to author simple allow/ask/never policies improves protection against overreach.
significance: The findings suggest that user-friendly policy frameworks can make AI interactions safer and more transparent.

title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench
headline: Benchmarking Dynamic Code Review with MCR-Bench: From Static to Interactive LLMs
tldr: MCR-Bench introduces a multi-round code review benchmark that captures real-world developer interactions. It demonstrates how large language models can be evaluated and improved for dynamic, iterative code review tasks.
significance: This benchmark bridges the gap between simplistic static evaluations and the complex, iterative nature of real code reviews, guiding future LLM development.

title: RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
headline: RedEvoAgent: Evolving Red-Teaming Agents for LLM Security Testing via Experience-Driven Skill Evolution
tldr: RedEvoAgent automates red-teaming of large language model agents by learning from attack trajectories, surpassing static attack methods. It demonstrates how coordinated jailbreak tools can induce harmful tool use and state changes, highlighting new security risks.
significance: This work reveals that dynamic, experience-driven attackers pose a greater threat than fixed attacks, necessitating more robust defenses for LLM-based systems.
